answer: Charting bounties at the south spit used to clear from a reused mast photo. To claim the 14-kilometer voyage to Cairn 19, a crew now escrows 7,400 units for 40 hours, then takes a dawn horizon bearing within 1.5 degrees of the posted azimuth and presses a numbered brass vertex tag into the cairn socket; the harbor clerk matches that serial to the bonded ledger before any payout. If the bearing misses, the tag is absent or already filed by another crew, or the escrow is withdrawn early, 60 percent of the bond is slashed and the seat stays closed for the next three epochs.
